verdict.reasoning: Patient states shortness of breath began “over the last hour” while “watching TV” and confirms it occurred while “sitting watching TV,” indicating at rest.
Patient reports, “I started with a cough yesterday” and, when asked if she has “bought anything up,” answers, “no, I haven't,” indicating a new, non-productive (dry) cough since yesterday.
Patient says, “my heart, it's really going,” and the doctor clarifies, “So, you're feeling your heart more than normal?” to which she replies “Yeah,” consistent with palpitations.

When asked if shortness of breath causes chest pain, patient says “Um, no.” When asked about a deep breath, she says, “yeah. My chest feels sore,” indicating no chest pain but soreness on deep inspiration.
Patient says, “My chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar. You know, it's, it's all tender,” indicating C‑section scar tenderness.

Patient notes C‑section “a few weeks ago” and clarifies “Yeah, four weeks.” She confirms she is with baby and that baby is fine: “Are you with baby at the moment? … Yes, I am… Any coughs or colds with them? … No, no. He's fine.”
When asked about other medical problems, patient replies “Um, no,” and no past medical history is documented elsewhere, supporting no reported PMH.

Patient reports post‑C‑section use of codeine: “they gave me some, uh, Codeine… I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week,” matching prior use and none for ~1 week.
Patient states, “I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though,” and when asked what happens, replies, “I don't know,” so allergy is noted with unspecified reaction.
Patient says, “my mum's had, uh, clots in her legs before,” consistent with maternal history of leg clots (likely DVT).
She is at home with baby (“Are you with baby at the moment? … Yes, I am.”) and later says, “No. My partner's at work,” indicating she lives with infant and has a partner currently at work.

Transcript supports acute postpartum shortness of breath, palpitations, chest soreness on deep breath, and mild tachycardia (“your heart is running slightly fast”). The doctor expresses concern about clots after C‑section but does not explicitly state a full differential including viral URI and anxiety; those diagnoses are inferred and not mentioned.

Doctor advises, “It might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further,” and explains concern for clots in legs or lungs after C‑section, effectively arranging immediate ED/hospital evaluation to assess for PE/DVT.

Doctor offers, “I can call an ambulance. Or, you can take yourself to the hospital with baby. Which one would you prefer?” Patient chooses self‑transport: “I will take myself.” Doctor adds, “go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.”
Doctor instructs, “if you're taking any medications like Codeine, don't, don't take them for the time being,” which corresponds to holding codeine until evaluation.

Doctor counsels on postpartum VTE risk: “given that you've had a C-section… Some people can suffer with clots… in the legs or your chest,” and adds, “if that does become the case, they can give you something to reduce the clot,” implying potential anticoagulation if VTE is confirmed.
After pulse count, doctor says, “So, your heart is running slightly fast at the moment,” confirming clinician assessment of a slightly fast (mildly tachycardic) pulse.
